obs_text: Strife: where it comes from, what holds it, what ends it.
Where anger is kept, devised and planned

Face 4Y. Strife and quarrel between people: Hits / verses: 8 / 8; Who, and at whom: the one who sows discord, the quarrelsome man, the meddler, a backbiting tongue; Abram and Lot; Example verses: Gen 13:8; Pro 6:14; Pro 18:19; Pro 26:21.

perverted heart → sowing discord (Pro 6:14); quarrelsome man → kindling strife (26:21); no whisperer → quarreling ceases (26:20); tarry over wine → strife, wounds (23:29–30); backbiting tongue → angry looks (25:23); no strife, for we are kinsmen → choose the land (Gen 13:8–9).

Where it comes from: The angry person: "A hot-tempered man stirs up strife" (15:18); "A man of wrath stirs up strife, and one given to anger causes much transgression" (29:22); The evil heart: "with perverted heart devises evil, continually sowing discord" (6:14); The tongue: a backbiting tongue (25:23), and the whisperer (26:20, 22); Wine: "Who has strife? Who has complaining? … Those who tarry long over wine" (23:29–30).

Seat: In the verse: Pro 6:14 "heart". The sower's own. Genuine. The heart is where discord is devised before it is sown. Pro 25:23 "wind". Spurious; Outside the verse: Pro 26:23 "fervent lips with an evil heart". Genuine. The whisperer's.
(v2) Pro 6:14: Seat word (Strong's as tagged): "heart" lev (H3820A); Phenomenon: SK §21; Whose seat: the sower's own, where discord is devised; Seat-sense check: genuine; Already read in: D v2 §2.2.

Part C: Zec 10:3. "My anger is hot against the shepherds, and I will punish the leaders." This follows "the household gods utter nonsense … they tell false dreams and give empty consolation. Therefore the people wander like sheep; they are afflicted for lack of a shepherd" (10:2): The leaders' failure leaves the people without a shepherd. Compare §20's kings who "made Israel to sin", and Isa 9:16 in §36.

13. Encouragement and building up (M52): "the church … walking in the fear of the Lord and in the comfort of the Holy Spirit, it multiplied" (Act 9:31) [D1]; "waiting for the consolation of Israel, and the Holy Spirit was upon him" (Luk 2:25) [D1]; "strive to excel in building up the church" (1Co 14:12); "building yourselves up … praying in the Holy Spirit" (Jude 20); "being built up as a spiritual house" (1Pe 2:5)

6.4 Hope and the NT inner seat: "my heart was glad … my flesh also will dwell in hope" (Act 2:26) — flesh in hope; "hope does not put us to shame, because God's love has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit" (Rom 5:5) [D1]; "by the power of the Holy Spirit you may abound in hope" (Rom 15:13) [D1]; "through the Spirit, by faith, we ourselves eagerly wait for the hope of righteousness" (Gal 5:5) [D3]; "one body and one Spirit … one hope" (Eph 4:4) [D1]; "the eyes of your hearts enlightened, that you may know what is the hope" (Eph 1:18); "in your hearts honor Christ … a reason for the hope that is in you" (1Pe 3:15); "waiting for the consolation of Israel, and the Holy Spirit was upon him" (Luk 2:25) [D1]

How it co-exists: No one left to help: "There is none to guide her among all the sons she has borne" (Isa 51:18); "who will console you? … who will comfort you?" (51:19); "drunk, but not with wine" (51:21); Humiliation: "you have made your back like the ground and like the street for them to pass over" (51:23); The community lament uses the same image: "you have given us wine to drink that made us stagger".

As a child's: "that you may nurse and be satisfied from her consoling breast; that you may drink deeply with delight … you shall be carried upon her hip, and bounced upon her knees. As one whom his mother comforts, so I will comfort you" (Isa 66:11–13). The figure is a child's delight at being fed and dandled. The comforting in the last line is God's own, as a mother's. I read the delight as one that is received, not worked for. It goes to *Thirst answered*, with a note to 13.1.
